title: Google Ads for Homestays and Small Resorts
excerpt: A practical Google Ads setup for homestays and small resorts: brand and destination campaigns, negative keywords, source-city targeting, assets and booking tracking.
description: Google Ads for homestays and small resorts: brand and destination campaigns, negative keywords, source-city targeting, call assets and booking tracking.
html:
Google Ads for a homestay or small resort works best with a few tight campaigns: a brand campaign for your own name, destination campaigns for searches like "homestay in Coorg", strong negative keywords, location targeting by the cities guests travel from, call and WhatsApp-friendly assets, and conversion tracking that counts enquiries and bookings, not clicks.

Why search ads suit small stays

Unlike social media ads, search ads appear when someone is already looking. A person typing "homestay near Chikmagalur with estate view" on a Thursday evening is probably planning a weekend trip. The challenge is that OTAs, aggregators and larger hotels bid on the same searches, so a small property has to be precise: show up for the right searches, in the right cities, at the right times, and send people somewhere that makes it easy to enquire.

Before you start, make sure your website has clear room pages, real photos, your phone and WhatsApp number, and a working enquiry form. If not, start with our guide to homestay website SEO and get the pages in place first.

A simple campaign structure

CampaignWhat it targetsWhy
BrandYour property name and its misspellingsProtects guests who already know you from being caught by OTA or competitor ads
Destination"homestay in <place>", "cottage near <place>", "estate stay <place>"Reaches people choosing where to stay
Feature or theme"pet friendly homestay <place>", "homestay with pool <place>", "family homestay <place>"Matches searches where you have a real advantage
Seasonal (optional)"<place> long weekend stay", "<place> monsoon stay"Runs only around peak or off-season pushes

Keep each campaign small and focused, with ad groups of closely related keywords and ads that repeat the searched idea in the headline.

The brand campaign

If guests search your name and an OTA ad appears above your own listing, some will book through the OTA. A brand campaign usually costs little because your name is highly relevant to your own site, and it lets you show your direct-booking value-adds, such as included breakfast or flexible changes.

Destination keywords

Use phrase and exact match for your main destination terms so ads show for searches close to what you intend. Broad match can find new searches but needs careful monitoring and good conversion data; for a small budget, start narrow and widen later.

Negative keywords: where small budgets are saved

Negative keywords stop your ads from showing for searches you do not want. For homestays, a starting list often includes:

  • Jobs and business: job, jobs, vacancy, salary, franchise, for sale, lease, rent monthly.
  • Information only: wiki, history, map only, weather (unless you sell on it).
  • Wrong type: hostel, dormitory, PG, paying guest, luxury 5 star, if you are none of those.
  • Free and DIY: free, camping free, how to start a homestay, homestay registration.
  • Other places: nearby destinations you are not close to, which Google sometimes matches anyway.

Check the search terms report every week for the first month, then fortnightly. Add any irrelevant search you find as a negative. This is the single most useful habit in a small account.

Location targeting by source city

A common mistake is to target people physically in your destination. Most of your guests are still at home when they book. Instead:

  • Use your booking records to list the cities your guests come from: for example Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad for a Coorg or Ooty property; Mumbai and Pune for Lonavala or Konkan; Delhi NCR and Chandigarh for Himachal.
  • Target those cities, and check your location setting so ads show to people located in them, not just people who have shown interest in them.
  • Consider a separate campaign, with a different message, for people near your destination searching on the day, such as "homestay near me tonight".
  • Schedule ads for the hours and days your enquiries actually come in, and raise budgets in the weeks before long weekends.

Call, WhatsApp and other assets

Assets (previously called extensions) add useful information to your ads. For a homestay:

  • Call asset: shows your number so mobile searchers can tap to call. Only enable it during hours someone answers.
  • Sitelinks: links to rooms, how to reach, food and experiences, and contact.
  • Callouts: short facts such as "Home-cooked meals", "Pet friendly", "Free parking".
  • Location asset: links your Google Business Profile so your address and reviews can appear.
  • WhatsApp: Google has offered message options in some markets, but availability changes. If a WhatsApp asset is not available in your account, link a sitelink or landing page button to your WhatsApp chat instead.

Google Hotel Ads and free booking links, in general terms

When people search for stays in Google Search or Maps, Google can show a hotel results panel with prices and booking options from different sites. Some of these are paid placements (Hotel Ads) and some are free booking links. Properties usually take part through a connectivity partner, such as a booking engine or channel manager that sends live rates and availability to Google.

For a small homestay without a booking engine, this is often a later step. If you use a booking engine or channel manager, ask the provider whether they support Google's hotel listings and what is required. Do not assume prices or eligibility; check with Google and your provider directly.

Track bookings, not clicks

Clicks are what you pay for, not what you want. Set up conversion tracking so Google Ads knows which clicks led to enquiries, and then match those to bookings.

  1. Track enquiries on the site: form submissions, clicks on the WhatsApp button, and clicks on the phone number, set up as conversions in Google Ads or through Google Analytics.
  2. Track calls from ads: use Google's call reporting where available, so calls from the call asset are counted.
  3. Label enquiries by source: ask every enquiry how they found you, and note "Google ad" in your booking sheet.
  4. Calculate cost per booking: monthly ad spend divided by the number of paid bookings from ads.

Example, for illustration only: a month with ₹10,000 of spend, 50 tracked enquiries and 5 paid bookings gives a cost per enquiry of ₹200 and a cost per booking of ₹2,000. Compare that with your average booking value and margin before deciding to scale. Our PPC management page explains how a fuller setup works.

Frequently asked questions

Should a homestay bid on its own name in Google Ads?

Often yes. If OTAs or competitors show ads on your name, a brand campaign keeps your own website at the top and lets you mention direct-booking value-adds. Brand clicks are usually inexpensive because your ad and site are highly relevant to the search. Review the search terms regularly to make sure the campaign shows only for your name and close variations.

What are negative keywords and why do they matter?

Negative keywords tell Google not to show your ad for certain searches, such as "jobs", "for sale", "hostel" or "free". Small budgets are easily used up by irrelevant searches, so a good negative list and a weekly look at the search terms report protect your money. Add negatives whenever you spot a search that would never become a booking.

Should I target people in my destination or in their home city?

Mostly their home city, because most guests book before they travel. Use your booking records to find the cities your guests come from and target those. A small, separate campaign for people already near your destination can catch last-minute searches, but it needs its own message and budget, and someone available to answer calls quickly.

Can a small homestay appear in Google Hotel Ads?

Possibly, but usually through a connectivity partner such as a booking engine or channel manager that sends your live rates and availability to Google. Without one, it is harder to take part. Ask your booking engine or channel manager whether they support Google's hotel listings, and check Google's current requirements before planning around it.

Where to start

Set up conversion tracking for form submissions, WhatsApp clicks and calls before spending anything. Then launch a brand campaign and one destination campaign, targeted to your top two source cities, with a starter negative keyword list. Check the search terms every week for a month and calculate your cost per booking at the end. For the social side of paid ads, read our guide to Meta ads for homestays.
